title: ‘We Have No Shared Reality’: Two Political Influencers on the Future of Politics Online
gist: A YouGov survey cited by WIRED finds nearly 65% of 2,000 US adults (77% of Gen Z) get political information from digital creators rather than traditional news. At the WIRED World Fair, Democrat Kat Abughazaleh and Republican strategist CJ Pearson clashed over the Trump administration's creator-first media strategy but agreed algorithms are creating partisan echo chambers among young Americans.

insights.claim: A recent YouGov survey of 2,000 US adults found nearly 65 percent get political information from digital creators, rising to 77 percent among Gen Z.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Attention and political ad spend are shifting from legacy news outlets to creator platforms, especially for younger audiences.

insights.claim: The Trump administration opened formal White House press briefings to digital creators and held influencer-specific briefings under former press secretary Karoline Leavitt, while restricting traditional media access, and multiple federal agencies now copy the playbook, per CJ Pearson.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Government institutionalizing creator access further erodes legacy media's privileged position and business model.

insights.claim: CJ Pearson argues the administration's creator strategy is simply the cost of capturing attention given short attention spans, though he called distributing parts of the Epstein files to 15 right-wing creators 'a misstep'.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Even supporters see execution risk in creator-led government communications.
insights.quote: It’s a very chronically online administration

insights.claim: Kat Abughazaleh argues the White House's embrace of 'AI slop and brutality', such as ICE-action ads, turns 'cruelty into content' rather than informing people and is designed to degrade attention spans.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Generative AI political content is a growing reputational and moderation issue for platforms.
insights.quote: They’re trying to ruin your attention span

insights.claim: Pearson claimed Elon Musk turned X into a 'bastion of free speech', a point Abughazaleh disputed, reflecting partisan divergence over platform governance.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: X's perceived partisan alignment shapes its user base and advertiser appeal.

insights.claim: Both Pearson and Abughazaleh agree that reliance on recommendation algorithms is creating echo chambers among young Americans of both parties, leaving no shared reality.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Bipartisan concern about algorithmic polarization raises the odds of future regulation of recommendation systems.
